- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast should be slightly below trend; if below, slightly above — align with sentiment direction.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27–0.80), model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use 5-day sentiment average to weight forecast adjustments.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true volatility in late period (last 7–10 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
